rationale: Base station storage was at 100% with loop recording disabled, triggering error E-402, which stops new event clips from being recorded — explaining the three-week gap in footage. After enabling loop recording, a test event immediately produced a new clip, confirming the fix resolved the issue. No account compromise is indicated; the missing recordings were due to full local storage, not deletion.

repair_steps: Confirm loop recording is enabled on the base station (Base Station Settings > Storage > Loop Recording).
Ask customer to trigger a test event and verify a new clip appears in playback.
Advise customer that old clips will be overwritten as new events are recorded; if they need to keep any existing clips, export them before they are overwritten.

complaint: The system stopped saving event clips. A break-in attempt happened at a neighbour's house, so I wanted to check my camera footage and there is nothing for the last three weeks! Did somebody delete my recordings? Is my account hacked? I haven't received any password-change emails.
usability_reason: The response is clear, polite, and actionable, and it accurately reflects the session: loop recording was enabled and a test event confirmed new clips are saving. It avoids unsupported claims about hacking or deleted recordings. Minor deduction because the customer reply says 'I've enabled loop recording' (the customer performed it) and the repair steps include 'Close the case as resolved' without explicit confirmation, but overall it is well-supported and usable.
